lessonsProposed: Camera regression tests should assert collision clearance and minimum avatar distance together; asserting only one invariant can conceal a forced move through geometry.

findings.trigger: When every candidate camera direction has less than 0.45 m of clear space, such as a tight corner or sealed pocket, sol.t is below HARD_MIN divided by the desired-ray length.
findings.consequence: Math.max forces the camera beyond the first reported blocker, placing it inside or through geometry even though the module's documented invariant says a position inside a collider is never an option.
findings.evidence: Line 366 correctly caps the normal distance floor at sol.t, but line 369 then takes Math.max with HARD_MIN/len, which exceeds sol.t in this case. The committed test at followCamera.test.ts:126-133 uses a query that always reports an immediate hit and checks only that camera distance is at least 0.45 m; it never checks the reported clear distance, so all 635 tests pass while accepting the collision.
findings.rule: Camera collision resolution must never place the camera beyond the solved clear distance, and a regression test must assert both obstacle clearance and body-distance invariants.
